tone_statements.citation: Adinlewa, Bisodun. 2024. Morphology of Àyèré, Kogi state Nigeria. World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews 24(2): 1200–1207. doi:10.30574/wjarr.2024.24.2.3379 (also Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.15094039).
tone_statements.quote: A tonal change in À yè re refers to the alteration of the pitch (or tone) of a syllable or a word, which can lead to changes in meaning. [...] Below are examples of how tonal change is used to form new words in À yè re A gbé “abuse” gbẹ “tin” gbè “Plant” B hé “tie” hè “warm” hẹ “deny” C ù nú “smell” ú nú “mushroom” ù nù “tongue” D ú ná “hell” [...] ú nà “trek” ù nà “journey / trip”
tone_statements.locator: p. 1204, section 1.4 'Tone Change' ('À yè re' spacing is a font-extraction artefact for Àyèré)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone, three-way contrast on the syllable (high á / mid unmarked / low à) shown by minimal triplets; tone also used derivationally ('tone change'); consistent with the 'three level tones' of the ELAR deposit note and PHOIBLE; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Allison, Idris Olawale. 2017. Vowel Deletion and Insertion in Úwù. Journal of Language and Education (HSE, Moscow) 3(2): 19–29. doi:10.17323/2411-7390-2017-3-2-19-29 (article header prints doi:10.17323/2411-7390-2017-3-2-19-38; both registered in Crossref).
tone_statements.quote: We observe that, such autosegmental features like tone (specifically high tone) (e.g. iii), nasality (e.g. xv), and roundness features (e.g. xi) usually persist only to realign with other segments within their environments. [...] Other salient observations are the cases of vowel lengthening, the High-Low (HL) tone sequence on the lengthened vowels and the low tone on the epenthetic vowel [i/u] that ensures that a nativised English word conforms to the open syllable structure of the Uwu language.
tone_statements.locator: paragraph after example (xv) (print p. ~22); and 'Results and Discussion' paragraph on loanword insertion (print p. ~27)
tone_statements.summary: Tonal (H vs L vs unmarked-mid marking in data); H-tone stability under V1 deletion; HL on loan lengthened vowels; inventory not stated here.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 1-2) gives only a 7-vowel chart and a consonant chart; the heading 3.3 'Tones' has no text under it; secs 2, 4, 5 are likewise empty. The Olumorin 1961 wordlist (pp. 3-24) carries partial tone marks (ígwú, adòdó, uyɛ́, iwɔ́wɔ́). a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing. downloaded via the Internet Archive (rogerblench.info blocks automated download with a captcha); 2015 and 2025 captures byte-identical.

sources.citation: Choon, Anja (depositor). 2007-2010. Documentation of Uwu, an endangered and undocumented minority language of the Nigerian Middle Belt. ELAR deposit dk0231 (formerly elar.soas.ac.uk/deposit/0231), SOAS.
sources.note: Deposit description (read via direct download; Preservica JS challenge blocks a raw save) states: 'Ayere has three level tones (and maybe glide tones and grammatical tones as well)', (V)CV syllables, syllabic nasal n/ŋ/m, Yoruba-like vowel harmony. No mention of stress or accent; no phonology write-up listed among the materials; cites Olumorin 1961, Blench 2006, Capo 1989.

sources.quote: A tonal change in À yè re refers to the alteration of the pitch (or tone) of a syllable or a word, which can lead to changes in meaning. [...] Below are examples of how tonal change is used to form new words in À yè re A gbé “abuse” gbẹ “tin” gbè “Plant” B hé “tie” hè “warm” hẹ “deny” C ù nú “smell” ú nú “mushroom” ù nù “tongue” D ú ná “hell” [...] ú nà “trek” ù nà “journey / trip”

sources.note: Sec. 1.4 'Tone Change' (p. 1204) treats tone as phonemic and derivational and gives minimal tone sets on identical segments marked high (acute), mid (unmarked) and low (grave): gbé 'abuse' / gbẹ 'tin' / gbè 'plant'; hé 'tie' / hè 'warm' / hẹ 'deny'; ùnú 'smell' / únú 'mushroom' / ùnù 'tongue'; úná 'hell' / únà 'trek' / ùnà 'journey'. 'Tone change' is also listed among the phonological criteria for wordhood (p. 1203). No explicit count of tonemes, no tone rules; all data tone-marked. No phonology section otherwise (morphology paper).

sources.citation: Allison, Idris Olawale. 2017. Vowel Deletion and Insertion in Úwù. Journal of Language and Education (HSE, Moscow) 3(2): 19–29. doi:10.17323/2411-7390-2017-3-2-19-29 (article header prints doi:10.17323/2411-7390-2017-3-2-19-38; both registered in Crossref).
sources.quote: We observe that, such autosegmental features like tone (specifically high tone) (e.g. iii), nasality (e.g. xv), and roundness features (e.g. xi) usually persist only to realign with other segments within their environments. [...] Other salient observations are the cases of vowel lengthening, the High-Low (HL) tone sequence on the lengthened vowels and the low tone on the epenthetic vowel [i/u] that ensures that a nativised English word conforms to the open syllable structure of the Uwu language.
sources.locator: paragraph after example (xv) (print p. ~22); and 'Results and Discussion' paragraph on loanword insertion (print p. ~27)
sources.note: No tone inventory statement or tone section; tone enters the analysis as an autosegment — high tone (also nasality, rounding) survives vowel elision and re-links (tone stability, autosegmental treatment), nativised English loans get an HL sequence on lengthened vowels and a low tone on the epenthetic [i/u]; all Úwù data are tone-marked (acute/grave/unmarked). Cites the author's 2015 EKSU MA thesis 'Aspects of the phonology of Uwu' as the fuller description.
